Resolves #21268

A button with a shared tooltip now shows it inside a dialog under `document.body`, whether or not the dialog has a `parentComponent`, and keeps it through the dialog's hide, show, close and reopen. The shared tooltip also listens on the root of each mounted target (`addDelegationRoot`, `delegateFromRootOf`). There is now one shared tooltip per browser window instead of one per app, so it renders in the window its target is in.

Evidence: L2 (a component spec in a real browser, red on `dev` and green on this head, plus unit arms for the per-window keying and release) → L2 required (the report reproduces with a browser hover in one window).

Change class: restoration (`fix`). agent-preflight: not hosted here; the lint-staged guards ran on the staged change.

| Sharing kept, `ownInstance` an explicit choice | CI-covered: one `.neo-tooltip` per hover in `FloatingRoot.spec.mjs`; `DelegationRoot.spec.mjs` pins one listener per root instance and one tooltip per root. The `ownInstance` branch is unchanged. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **A second gate.** With a `parentComponent`, the event did reach the main view's listener, but `DomEvent.verifyMouseEnterLeave()` looked for the target in the main view's vdom and dropped the mouseenter. Listening on the dialog itself passes both gates.
- **One shared tooltip per browser window, not per app.** An app can span several windows, and the per-app tooltip always rendered in the main view's window. Two apps in one window now share one tooltip, and each still anchors its main view there, because `data-neo-tooltip` targets (the Portal's examples list, `examples/toolbar/paging`) announce nothing. A window's tooltip is destroyed when the window's last port disconnects. `App#reapWindow` never reached it, since a floating tooltip is in no app's tree, and the per-app tooltip leaked the same way.
- **A target reaches its window's tooltip when it is created**, not first on mount, so no pointer reaches it before its root listens. The tooltip anchors a main view only once it is an instance. The first head anchored the main-view config of a second SharedWorker root (`addDomListeners is not a function`), which turned `CanvasGroupPainting` and `NoOpenerRootRendererKill` red in CI.
- **A root answers to one tooltip, and a tooltip takes its listeners and delays with it** (Round 1). A shared tooltip that takes a root releases it from the other windows' tooltips, so a root that moved windows stops reaching the one it left. A tooltip records its listeners per root and removes them when it is destroyed; it registers one listener per event, because `Neo.manager.DomEvent` removes a listener object under its last event key only. `destroy()` clears the show, hide and dismiss timers.
- The multi-window keying, release and teardown are pinned by unit arms. The two canvas specs above run a second root of the Portal app in a browser.
- Out of scope, noted in defect-notes: a target destroyed under the pointer stays the tooltip's `activeTarget`, so a new target with the same id shows nothing until the pointer leaves it once. That mechanism predates this PR, and `FloatingRoot.spec.mjs` moves the pointer away before closing the dialog, as reaching a close button does. Separately, `DomEvent#updateDomListeners()` removes any listener object with several event keys under its last key only; this PR no longer registers such an object.

## Test Evidence
Red-first, in a base worktree carrying only the new spec: on `dev` `fb5f004203` 4 failed (both dialog kinds, both arms) and the control passed. On `28295111d4`, the tooltip and dock-tooltip component specs (11) passed 4 runs in a row, `CanvasGroupPainting` and `NoOpenerRootRendererKill` passed 8/8, and the tooltip and component unit specs passed 249. Full unit tier on the first head: 7866 passed, 2 skipped.

Round 1, red-first in a base worktree at `28295111d4` carrying only the new unit spec: root transfer `[1,1]` on the window it left, root-first destruction `[1,0]`, tooltip-first destruction failed too, and a pending show at last-port departure ran on the destroyed tooltip (`[31,32]`, with the sibling window's `32` as the control). All four arms pass on `0933c59367`, as do the tooltip unit specs (18), the tooltip component specs in Chromium (9) and the full unit tier (7874 passed, 2 skipped).

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to review [5944474506](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21270#pullrequestreview-5944474506) (Round 1 at `28295111d4`). Both findings reproduced before the fix.

**Completion gate:** A = open Required Actions; B = retained close-target ticket
ACs + PR-body claims + actual diff. A is empty relative to B at this head.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Make shared-tooltip root registrations reversible and scoped to the root's current window. In `Tooltip#addDelegationRoot` and `destroy` (`src/tooltip/Base.mjs:97–109,256–264`), the live root retains its original listener scope when it moves, and Tooltip teardown removes only the worker observer and registry entry. Use independently removable enter and leave registrations through the existing DOM-event owner. Cover live-root transfer with only the destination tooltip receiving hover, and both root-first and tooltip-first destruction with zero residual callbacks.
      **Commit:** `0933c59367`
      **Details:** `addDelegationRoot` registers one `mouseenter` and one `mouseleave` listener through `addDomListeners` and records them per root. A shared tooltip that takes a root first releases it from the other windows' tooltips (`removeDelegationRoot` → `removeDomListeners`), and `destroy()` releases every live root it holds. Your root-first `[1,0]` has an engine cause: `DomEvent#updateDomListeners()` removes a listener object under its last event key only (`getEventName`), so the combined listener kept its `mouseenter`. Single-event listeners avoid that here; the engine asymmetry is out of scope, captured in a defect-note and named in the PR body. In `DelegationRoot.spec.mjs`, the transfer, root-first and tooltip-first arms assert the `DomEvent.items` registrations per tooltip (the set `fire()` dispatches from) at `[0,0]` after release, rather than dispatching a hover. Red-first at `28295111d4`: `[1,1]` on the window the root left, `[1,0]` after root-first destruction, and tooltip-first destruction failed as well.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Cancel tooltip delay work when the instance is destroyed. The new last-port path at `src/tooltip/Base.mjs:440–443` destroys an instance without retiring its raw timers. A pending show can then enter `initVnode()` on the destroyed object. Verify hover then last-port departure before the show delay, using a sibling window or a still-live port as the positive control.
      **Commit:** `0933c59367`
      **Details:** `destroy()` clears the show, hide and dismiss timers for every tooltip. The new arm arms a 20 ms show on the tooltips of windows 31 and 32, retires window 31's last port before the delay, and expects only window 32's show to run. It got `[31,32]` at `28295111d4` and gets `[32]` here.

The tooltip unit specs (18), the tooltip component specs in Chromium (9) and the full unit tier (7874 passed, 2 skipped) pass locally on `0933c59367`.
